question: The 2010 Hockey World Cup final took place in which Indian city?
solution:
The correct answer is __**New Delhi**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **2010 Men's Hockey World Cup** was the **12th edition** of the flagship international field hockey tournament organized by the **International Hockey Federation (FIH)**.
 
• The entire tournament was held from **28 February to 13 March 2010** at the **Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium** located in **New Delhi**, India.
 
• The final match was contested between **Australia** and **Germany** on **13 March 2010**, where **Australia** secured a **2-1** victory to claim the championship.
 
• This victory marked **Australia**'s second world title, their first being in **1986**, and ended **Germany**'s streak as the two-time defending champions.
 
• The tournament featured **12 participating nations**, and the final was the culminating event held in the heart of India's capital city.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium**:
 
 
• It is a premier sports venue named after the legendary Indian hockey player **Major Dhyan Chand**, often called 'The Wizard' of hockey.
 
• The stadium underwent significant renovation for the **2010 World Cup** and the **2010 Commonwealth Games**.
 
• It previously hosted the hockey competition during the **1951** and **1982 Asian Games**.
 
 
 
• **Tournament Highlights**:
 
 
• The **Netherlands** finished in third place, winning the **Bronze Medal** after defeating **England** with a score of **4-3**.
 
• **Guun Beins** (Netherlands) and **Luke Doerner** (Australia) were among the prominent goal scorers during the event.
 
• **India**, as the host nation, finished the tournament in **8th position**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**:
 
 
• This was the second time **India** hosted the **Men's Hockey World Cup**, with the first instance being in **1982** in **Mumbai**.
 
• Subsequent to this, India also hosted the **2018** and **2023** editions in **Bhubaneswar** and **Rourkela**.
